learn.title: Azure Policy and resource locks
objectives: Explain what Azure Policy does: create, assign and manage rules that keep resources compliant.
Recognise policy definitions, initiatives, assignments, scopes, exclusions and common effects.
Explain how Azure Policy evaluates new and existing resources and how remediation works.
Describe resource locks (CanNotDelete and ReadOnly), where they apply and how they are inherited.
Choose between Azure Policy, resource locks and RBAC for a governance requirement.
concepts: Azure Policy
A service that creates, assigns and manages rules (policies) that resources must follow, and reports whether resources comply.
Policy definition
A single rule, such as 'allowed locations' or 'require a tag', with an effect that says what happens when a resource doesn't comply.
Initiative
A group of related policy definitions managed and assigned as one unit, for example a security baseline.
Assignment
Applying a definition or initiative to a scope: management group, subscription, resource group or resource. Child scopes inherit it.
Effects
What a policy does: deny blocks non-compliant requests, audit logs non-compliance, modify/append changes properties, deployIfNotExists deploys a missing configuration.
Remediation
A task that brings existing non-compliant resources into compliance for policies with modify or deployIfNotExists effects.
Compliance view
Azure Policy evaluates resources when they are created or changed and on a regular cycle, and shows compliant and non-compliant resources.
Resource lock
A setting that stops resources being deleted or changed by mistake. It applies to every user, including Owners.
CanNotDelete lock
Shown as 'Delete' in the portal. Users can read and modify the resource but can't delete it.
ReadOnly lock
Users can read the resource but can't change or delete it. Some operations that look like reads, such as listing storage keys, are also blocked.
comparisons: Policy controls what resources and settings are allowed. Locks protect resources that already exist from deletion or change.
Policy decides what can be deployed and how it must be configured. RBAC decides who can perform which actions.
CanNotDelete still allows changes. ReadOnly allows neither changes nor deletion.
Deny blocks the non-compliant request. Audit allows it but flags the resource as non-compliant.
traps: A deny policy doesn't delete existing non-compliant resources; it reports them as non-compliant.
Locks override permissions: even an Owner must remove the lock before deleting the resource.
Locks protect the management plane, not data: a lock on a storage account doesn't stop blobs inside it being deleted.
Tags aren't inherited automatically, but a policy can add or inherit them.
An initiative is a group of policies, not a different kind of lock.
revision: Policy = rules for resources; initiative = bundle of policies; assignment = rules applied at a scope.
Scopes: management group > subscription > resource group > resource, with inheritance downward.
Deny blocks, audit reports, modify/append change, deployIfNotExists deploys.
Remediation tasks fix existing resources for modify and deployIfNotExists policies.
Locks: CanNotDelete (change OK, no delete) and ReadOnly (no change, no delete).
Locks apply to everyone, are inherited by child resources, and must be removed before the blocked action.

questions.on: Describe the purpose of Azure Policy
questions.q: What is the main purpose of Azure Policy?
opts: To create and enforce rules that Azure resources must follow, and report on compliance
To control which users can sign in to the Azure portal
To estimate the monthly cost of new resources
To store secrets and certificates securely
questions.e: Azure Policy enforces organisational standards on resources and shows which resources are non-compliant.

questions.on: Describe the purpose of Azure Policy
questions.q: In Azure Policy, what is a policy definition?
opts: A list of users allowed to manage a subscription
A billing report grouped by tag
A rule that describes a required condition for resources and the effect to apply when it isn't met
A backup copy of a resource's configuration

questions.on: Describe the purpose of Azure Policy
questions.q: What is an Azure Policy initiative?
opts: A report of last month's Azure spending
A collection of policy definitions grouped together and assigned as a single unit
A lock that prevents resources being deleted
A template that deploys virtual machines
questions.e: Initiatives (policy sets) simplify managing many related policies, such as a security or regulatory baseline.

questions.on: Describe the purpose of Azure Policy
questions.q: What does it mean to assign an Azure Policy?
opts: To attach the policy to a single user account
To give a user permission to edit the policy text
To schedule the policy to run once and then delete itself
To apply a policy definition or initiative to a specific scope so it takes effect there

A tag named Region on each resource

questions.on: Describe the purpose of Azure Policy

Tag every VM with its cost centre
Apply a CanNotDelete lock to each resource group
Ask Azure Advisor to send cost recommendations
questions.e: The built-in 'Allowed virtual machine size SKUs' policy denies VM sizes that aren't on the approved list.

questions.on: Describe the purpose of Azure Policy

2. Existing resources are re-evaluated on a regular compliance cycle.

Statement 3 only
Statements 1, 2 and 3
